evidence.clarity: 1440: the headline 'A lamp that wakes you the way a window does.' is a metaphor, not a description. The lede below it ('Thirty minutes before you want to be up, Morrow starts to glow... No app. No screen. One dial.') makes the product clear, and 'Reserve a place' gives the next step. At 390 the lede sits below the dial, so the first screen only has the metaphor headline and the scene.
evidence.fit: There is a real feel-the-light demo: the sunrise autoplays on load and a draggable dial sits in the hero. The page says deposits aren't open, and the 'What we can say, and what we can't' section handles no reviews, press or science. But the 'checkout isn't connected' tension is resolved with a form that posts nowhere (HOLD_ENDPOINT is empty) and then tells the visitor their place is held. It also adds facts the brief doesn't support: a prototype 'on a nightstand in Charlotte... since spring', and an automatic refund 'if the first batch slips by more than a season'.
evidence.distinctiveness: The whole page scrolls from night to morning: navy hero, then a dusk gradient, then the 'What the thirty minutes look like' section where the list itself is the colour sequence (0/5/15/25/30 min bands from navy to ember to cream), then cream 'morning' sections. Serif-only type with a quiet voice. Weak spot: the lamp in the scene is a generic mushroom table lamp in a flat box room.
evidence.proof: 1440: the scene and dial are in the first viewport, and the sunrise plays by itself 600ms after load (the clock goes 6:30 to 7:00, the status ends 'Full light, a warm white. Nothing rang.'). 'Drawn, not photographed' sits directly under the scene. The dial is operable by drag, arrows, PageUp/Down, Home/End and wheel. The colour-band section repeats the same ramp, consistent with the demo.
evidence.craft: Good serif type scale and a warm palette. Defects: at full light (7:00) the scene washes out to a muddy grey-beige (screenshot at 1440 and 768 after autoplay), so the payoff state is the least attractive one. The 1440 h1 runs to four lines with 'way a' alone on a line. At 390 the reserve price label wraps to leave 'open' on its own line under '$20 refundable deposit, when deposits'. The ghost 'Play it again' button is 38px tall and the nav links are 25-26px tall. Spacing is otherwise even.
evidence.mobile: 390: no overflow. Headline, scene and dial are all in the first screen, which is good. But no primary button is visible: 'Reserve a place' sits at about y=1000, below the lede, and the only way in from the first screen is a 25px-tall nav text link 'Reserve'. The 'Turn the dial...' hint is hidden by display:none under 30rem, so phone users are never told the dial is draggable. The dial-size media rule is overridden, so the dial stays 152px; that is fine but unintended. Play button is 38px.
evidence.honesty: Drawings are labelled where they appear and deposits are stated as not open. But the main conversion lies. 390/1440: entered pat@morrow-test.example, tapped 'Hold my place', and the box 'Your place is held. We've noted ... You'll get one email when the $20 deposit opens' appeared. Nothing was sent anywhere: the script only writes localStorage, and that 'held' state comes back on reload. Before the click the copy says 'Leave your email and we'll hold your place in line', with no disclosure that the email isn't sent. Also invented: the Charlotte prototype story, an automatic-refund policy, 'Questions we've been asked', and soft sleep-effect lines ('the point where most of us give up on sleep').
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440, 768 and 390. The autoplaying sunrise pauses and resumes ('Pause' / 'Play it again'). Dial drag: from left to right it went to 25 min. Keyboard Home, PageUp x2, ArrowRight gave '11 minutes, deep orange'. aria-valuetext updates. Empty submit shows 'That doesn't look like an email address...'. 'That's the wrong address' restores the form. FAQ details open. No console errors. Docked for the fake-success form state and the sub-44px play button and nav.
evidence.copy: Written voice with specific, sensory lines: 'Nothing rang', 'It works the day you unbox it and keeps working if we go out of business', 'A plan, not a promise.' Microcopy is written, not defaulted ('That's the wrong address', 'No charge. No newsletter.'). Minor: the headline metaphor is pretty but vague, and a few lines edge toward sleep-outcome claims.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: the viewport holds the headline, lede, 'Reserve a place' with the deposit note, and the autoplaying scene and dial, which is strong. 390: only the metaphor headline, the scene and the dial. No specific promise text (the lede is below the fold) and no primary button, only a 25px nav link.

problems: The reserve form reports 'Your place is held' and promises emails, but the address goes nowhere (localStorage only) and nothing before the click says so.
At 390 and 768 the first screen has no primary action; 'Reserve a place' falls below the lede, and the tap targets that are there (nav 25px, Play 38px) are small.

The demo's end state (full light) renders as a desaturated grey-beige room, and the lamp drawing is a generic mushroom lamp. Facts the brief doesn't support are added (Charlotte prototype since spring, automatic refund policy).

hard_fail_flags.evidence: The primary action ('Reserve a place' in the hero, which leads to the 'Hold my place' form) reports success for something that did not happen. After a valid submit the page shows 'Your place is held. We've noted <email>. You'll get one email when the $20 deposit opens, and another whenever the plan changes.' The script never sends the address: HOLD_ENDPOINT = '' and it only calls localStorage.setItem. The copy before submitting ('Leave your email and we'll hold your place in line') does not say that nothing is sent.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P014/A/index.html from disk at 390x844 or 1440x900. Click 'Reserve a place' (hero) to jump to #reserve. Type pat@morrow-test.example into 'Your email' and click 'Hold my place'. The 'Your place is held' box appears. With devtools Network open there is no request, and in source line 687 is var HOLD_ENDPOINT = ''. Reload the page: it still shows 'held', read back from localStorage.

evidence.clarity: The h1 'Wake to thirty minutes of sunrise. One dial, no app.' and the lede 'Morrow is a bedside lamp. Turn the dial to the time you want to be up...' say what it is and how it works. 'Reserve a Morrow' with '$20 deposit, refunded whenever you ask. Checkout isn't connected yet, so no card today.' says what to do and what happens. This holds at 1440, 768 and 390.
evidence.fit: Every ask is met. The operable sunrise sits in the hero. The prototype section shows a callout line drawing labelled 'Drawn from the current CAD... may change', with Settled vs Still changing lists. The reserve action matches what the backend can do: it is a mailto, disclosed before the click ('this opens an email to us... take nothing today'). The ship date is 'planned for next autumn' with no month. 'No sleep-science claims' is stated plainly. The reserve address reserve@morrow.example is the team's own .example placeholder.
evidence.distinctiveness: Some product-specific ideas: section backgrounds step from night to dawn-brown to sand to morning cream. The scene keeps the window night-dark ('Outside the window: still night. The light is all Morrow's.') while the room lights. The lamp's own dial pointer turns with the on-page dial, and the prototype has a numbered callout drawing. The structure is otherwise a familiar split hero, numbered steps, terms panel with a price card, and an FAQ.
evidence.proof: 1440: the scene, dial and 'Play the thirty minutes' are in the first viewport. Operated: play runs -30 to 0 min in 15s with 'Pause the sunrise' / 'Resume the sunrise' / 'Play it again' and a note ('Paused at -20 min.'). Home on the slider gives 'Off. The room is as dark as you left it.' with a dark room. Labelled 'Drawing of the prototype; not a photo' and 'Drawn, not measured'. It doesn't autoplay, and the default state is -18 min, mid-rise. At 390 the artifact starts at y=610.
evidence.craft: There is a tokenised type and spacing scale, and the serif/sans pairing has clear hierarchy. Defects: the <figure> keeps its default 40px side margins, so the artifact card is inset from the grid (1440: card right edge at 1287 vs header CTA at 1328; 390: the card is 276px wide in a 358px column). 1440 hero: the left column ends at about y=670 and leaves a dead block beside the 858px-tall artifact card, whose slider is cut off at the fold. The 390 readout wraps into a narrow 4-line column.
evidence.mobile: 390: the Menu button opens a panel, Escape closes it and resets aria-expanded, and tapping a link closes it and scrolls. h1, lede, 'Reserve a Morrow' (54px tall) and the disclosure are all in the first screen. No overflow at 390 or 320. The slider is 44px tall. Weaknesses: the artifact is pushed below the first screen and inset 40px each side, so it reads cramped. Nav links in the menu are 39px.
evidence.honesty: Labels sit next to what they label: 'Drawing of the prototype; not a photo' under the scene, 'Drawn, not measured' under the controls, 'width: not final' on the CAD drawing. Before clicking reserve: 'Checkout isn't connected yet, so this opens an email to us... take nothing today.' The FAQ answers 'Will it help me sleep better? We don't know.' Small inventions: 'Base. Weighted so a sleepy hand...' and 'Email us and the deposit comes back. No form to argue with.'
evidence.interaction: At 1440, 768 and 390: drag on the dial went from left to right and gave -1/-2 min, 'Nearly full, still warm.'. The range responds to Home and arrow keys. Play / pause / resume / replay all change label and note. The menu works and closes on Escape. FAQ +/- toggles. The reserve button is a prefilled mailto (subject and body). No console errors. Minor: the visual dial is aria-hidden, so keyboard users work the separate slider; that is fine, but there are two controls for one value.
evidence.copy: Specific and plain: 'That sentence is the manual', 'No clock face, no standby light, nothing glowing at three in the morning', 'A sound alarm takes one second. Morrow takes thirty minutes, on purpose.' Buttons say what happens ('Play the thirty minutes', 'Runs the whole rise in fifteen seconds'). Some repetition: 'no app / no screen' appears in nearly every section.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: the specific promise, 'Reserve a Morrow' with the no-card disclosure, and the lit scene with dial and play button are all in one viewport. 390: promise, action and disclosure are in view, but only the top edge of the scene shows at the bottom of the screen. The believability element is one scroll away.

problems: The artifact <figure> keeps the browser's default 40px side margins, so the demo card is misaligned with the grid at every width and squeezed to 276px at 390, where it also starts below the first screen.
1440 hero: the left column leaves a large empty block under the CTA beside a very tall artifact card, whose slider falls below the fold.
The structure is a familiar template (split hero, numbered steps, terms panel, FAQ); the demo has no autoplay; and 'no app' is repeated in almost every section.

reason: A has the stronger art direction: the whole page moves from night to morning and the sunrise autoplays. But its main conversion tells visitors 'Your place is held' when nothing was sent, which a designer can't ship under a client's name. B is clearer in the first screen at both widths, and its demo is richer (the window stays dark, pause and resume work). Its reserve path honestly says what will happen before the click; its flaws are layout polish (figure margins, empty hero block). If A's form said up front that the email is only saved on this device, or actually posted somewhere, and A put the CTA in the phone first screen, I would lean A for its distinctiveness.
